desc: Statutory touchpoints when you bring someone on board — coverage, registration, and offer documentation.

items.task: Check whether the establishment is covered by the Factories Act (10+ workers with power, 20+ without) and complete approval/licensing/registration if so.
Register the establishment under the OSH Code where required.
Register the establishment for social security (PF/ESI) coverage.
Confirm ESI applicability and contribution liability for new joiners.
Fix wages at or above the applicable minimum wage before making an offer.
For contract-labour hiring, use only licensed contractors and understand the effect of engaging through a non-licensed contractor.
If hiring inter-state migrant workers, note the principal employer's facility and registration duties.
For child/adolescent engagement, check age-based restrictions and fitness certificates.

name: Hiring & Recruitment

desc: Day-one to day-thirty: standing orders, registers, and statutory communication to the new employee.

items.task: Submit draft standing orders for certification where the establishment has 100+ workmen.
Communicate certified standing orders to every workman (they govern conduct, leave, termination).
Add the employee to statutory registers (e.g. register of adult workers).
Notify the occupier/establishment commencement details where required.
Enrol the employee for PF contributions and explain the employer/employee split.
Explain maternity benefit rights to eligible women employees at onboarding.
Cover safety duties, welfare facilities and emergency procedures during induction.

name: Onboarding & Induction

desc: Monthly payroll compliance — wages, deductions, contributions, bonus and gratuity accruals.

items.task: Pay wages on time and in the permitted mode; respect the wage-period rules.
Apply only authorised deductions (fines, absence, etc.) within statutory limits.
Compute overtime at double the ordinary rate where applicable.
Deposit PF contributions (employer + employee) on time.
Deposit ESI contributions where the establishment is covered.
Check annual bonus eligibility for each employee (20+ persons establishment).
Track continuous service for gratuity accrual (5 years, with exceptions).
Maintain wage registers and file required returns/notices.

name: Payroll & Compensation

desc: Resignation, retrenchment, dismissal or closure — the exit is where disputes start.

items.task: For retrenchment of workmen, satisfy the conditions precedent (notice, compensation, government intimation).
Under the IR Code, follow the retrenchment procedure and timelines for covered establishments.
Complete disciplinary proceedings within the statutory time limit before dismissal for misconduct.
Pay gratuity as soon as it becomes payable; determine the amount per the statutory formula.
Ensure no dismissal or punishment during an employee's sickness/maternity benefit period.
For closure of an undertaking, give the required 60 days' notice of intention.
Settle full and final dues including wages, leave encashment and bonus within timelines.

name: Separation & Termination

desc: Principal-employer duties when work is done through contractors.

items.task: Confirm whether the contract-labour Part applies (50+ contract labour on any day).
Obtain/renew the contractor licence through the prescribed procedure.
Never engage contract labour through a non-licensed contractor — know the legal effect.
Check whether contract labour is prohibited in the specific process/operation.
As principal employer, ensure welfare facilities for contract workers.
Ensure PF/ESI contributions are paid for contract employees (recover from contractor if needed).

name: Contract Labour Management

desc: Ongoing duties for a safe, lawful workplace — committees, facilities, accident reporting.

items.task: Constitute a Safety Committee and appoint safety officers where thresholds apply.
Provide statutory welfare facilities (washing, canteen, rest rooms, first aid).
Provide crèche facilities where the worker threshold is met.
Report accidents and dangerous occurrences to the authorities within timelines.
Maintain safety records, registers and file returns.
Cooperate with Inspector-cum-Facilitators; know their powers.
Review the general penalty provisions so the cost of non-compliance is visible to management.

name: Workplace Safety & Welfare
